name: Why So High
tagline: Snap your electricity bill. Why So High tells you why it went up and what you can do about it this month.
scope: AEP Ohio residential customers in Columbus, Ohio

entry_points.check_in_two_minutes: npm install && npm run demo && npm run eval && npm test
entry_points.web: npm run web:build && npm run serve, then http://127.0.0.1:8787
entry_points.your_own_bill_photo: POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/api/photo, or 'Read your own bill' on the page (live stack only)
entry_points.http: POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/api/run with a request like input_examples/example_1.json
entry_points.evaluation: npm run eval && npm run eval:billreader && npm run eval:explainer

sample_mode: SAMPLE_MODE=true is the default with no .env. The agent code runs unchanged on model and SQL responses recorded from a live run in samples/cache/. A new request with bill fields also runs: its weather join is computed from the NOAA copy in data/snapshot/ and logged as source snapshot. A bill image that was never recorded needs the live stack.

agents.name: BillReader
agents.role: Reads the bill photo into fields with Nemotron 3.5 Super VL; falls back to the bill's text layer with a Nemotron text model

agents.name: WeatherAnalyst
agents.role: Joins the household's bills with NOAA daily weather in one federated Zetaris query and fits or picks the weather model

agents.name: RateAnalyst
agents.role: Recomputes the bill from AEP Ohio's tariff versions in OpenEI URDB, read through Zetaris; reads Ohio's average price from EIA through Zetaris as context

agents.name: UsageAnalyst
agents.role: Splits the dollar change into price, extra days, weather, own use and unexplained

agents.name: ReconciliationCritic
agents.role: Runs checks 1 to 6 and sends work back with the reason when one fails, including the Explainer's sentences

agents.name: ActionPlanner
agents.role: Proposes assistance programs and actions with amounts from the household's facts

agents.name: Explainer
agents.role: Writes the accepted split in plain words with Nemotron; check 6 verifies every number

agents.name: HouseholdMemory
agents.role: Meterless H-MEM and World Model: diagnoses, what the household tells us, and the household graph with provenance

agents.name: Orchestrator
agents.role: Runs the steps in order, routes the checker's send-backs, and writes the accepted decision back through Zetaris

models.used_by: BillReader (text-layer fallback); the model the Explainer asks for
The model both evaluation baselines ask for

agent_framework: None. The orchestrator is plain TypeScript.

sponsor_technology.zetaris: Federated SQL over the sources in place, in both directions: every run joins the household bills in Postgres with NOAA NCEI daily weather (REST) in one query, reads AEP Ohio's tariff versions from OpenEI URDB (REST), reads Ohio's average residential price from the EIA API (REST, nested rows unpacked with LATERAL VIEW explode), and writes each accepted decision back into household_pg.decisions with INSERT, then reads it back. Sources: src/zetaris/sources.ts; queries: src/zetaris/queries.ts, decisions.ts, statePrice.ts.
sponsor_technology.meterless: Nightshift serves every model call (src/llm/nightshift.ts) and its compute receipt (receipt id, route, consensus, cross-checks) is kept in the trace and shown on the page. H-MEM and World Model, vendored unchanged in engines/, hold the household's memory, and that memory changes the diagnosis and the action plan.
sponsor_technology.nvidia: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL reads the bill photo, a Nemotron text model writes the plain-words summary that check 6 verifies, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning reads the text layer when vision fails, and Nemotron 3 Ultra is the model both evaluation baselines ask for.
sponsor_technology.cursor: Not used. The code was written with Claude Code (Anthropic). The organizers' HackOS FAQ lists Cursor as optional.

data_sources.name: NOAA NCEI daily summaries, Columbus station USW00014821
EIA retail sales API
data_sources.use: Ohio's average residential price on every run; the statewide weather prior, fitted once on Jan 2025 to Jul 2026

data_sources.name: EIA RECS 2020, table CE4.3
data_sources.use: Heating slope of electric-heat homes in the evaluation generator

data_sources.name: ODJFS, PUCO and AEP Ohio program pages, read 22 Oct 2026
data_sources.use: Program amounts, income limits and dates in src/actions/programs.ts
data_sources.license: Public program information, cited per value

data_sources.name: Linda's household and bills
data_sources.license: Synthetic, generated from the published tariff by scripts/make-sample-bill.ts

served_by.note: Nightshift's router chose the model that answered; counts over parsed answers.

bill_reader.note: One synthetic bill layout; the photos are simulated with scripts/photo-bills.py, not photos of real bills

evaluation.ablation_note: Same code with one piece removed: no closure check sending the first split back, or Ohio averages instead of the household's fitted weather model. The truth is also calibrated to the previous bill.

pre_existing_components: Meterless H-MEM and World Model engines (Apache-2.0), vendored unchanged from github.com/Meterless/Meterless at commit 1742dec, listed in engines/VENDORED.md
routing_note: Nightshift's router chooses the model that answers; the trace logs the model asked for, the model that answered and the Meterless compute receipt on every call.
